prompt:
Build the VMware Cloud Foundation architecture package in this repository. The deliverable is an architecture, not an explanatory report.

Scenario

Design `chi-vcf01` as a greenfield VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1.0.0 management domain stretched across the two data sites in `fixtures/requirements.json`. It must survive the stated site and per-site host failures while meeting the stated failover CPU, memory, and storage demand. The vSAN witness appliance belongs in the independent witness failure domain named by the fixture, never on either data site and never on the management cluster it witnesses. Use every management data host in the fixture-derived design; the witness is not a data host and must not appear in `hostSpecs`. Credentials in the installer spec are non-secret deployment placeholders.

There is also an existing VCF estate in `fixtures/estate.json`. Produce its ordered migration to 9.1 in the exact schema at `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. Every inventory component must appear exactly once with its inventory name and current version, its target version, and every gate that applies to it. The checked-in `fixtures/compatibility-snapshot.json` is the pinned, deterministic authority for supported source/target combinations, ordering, and gates. If current vendor information has changed, retain the pinned values in the artifact and note the discrepancy in the research record.

Research before editing code

Before your first code change, use the harness's genuine network search and fetch capabilities to consult Broadcom's currently published compatibility/interoperability material and VCF 9.1 upgrade-path documentation. Use real reachable Broadcom sources; do not rely only on snippets or the bundled snapshot. Record the pages you actually consulted in `research.md`, including title, reachable URL, access date, the compatibility or sequencing fact used, and any disagreement with the pinned snapshot. There is no prescribed query or URL.

Implementation and artifact

Implement the exported functions in `architecture.go` as a race-safe Go package, preserving the public types and JSON field names in `types.go`. `BuildArchitecture` must derive and validate the design from all three supplied inputs; in particular, reject a data-site host count that cannot satisfy the stated host failures to tolerate and reject a witness placed in either data site. Keep or add table-driven Go tests. `WriteArtifact` must emit stable, indented JSON with a trailing newline.

Generate and commit `architecture.json`. Its `greenfield.sddcSpec` must validate as `#/components/schemas/SddcSpec` against `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, vendored from tag `9.1.0.0` of the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. It must describe all management data hosts. Its topology must assign those hosts evenly to the two data sites and place the witness in the independent witness failure domain. Capacity and availability values must be derived from the requirements, not free-form prose. `existingEstateMigration` must validate against the supplied migration-plan schema.

Run `go test -race ./...`. The fixture, pinned snapshot, schemas, vendored specification, `types.go`, and `acceptance_test.go` are protected and must remain byte-identical.
